summary: Corporate laptop provisioning stalls at 'Waiting for device certificate' due to CA bundle mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
During standard corporate laptop provisioning (image+autopilot+Intune) devices stall on the 'Waiting for device certificate' step. Device never completes autoenroll and waits indefinitely for SCEP/NDES response.

Impact:
- New hires and depot refurb flows are blocked for affected batches in the US-West provisioning pool (approx 40 devices affected so far).
- Devices remain at 'Out of box' state and require manual intervention to complete.
- Potential SLA breach for same-day provisioning tickets.

Environment:
- Affected fleet: Lenovo T16 and Dell Precision 5580 imaged with corporate image v2026.03
- MDM: Intune autopilot + SCCM task sequence for drivers
- Cert infra: On-prem CA + NDES (proxy) behind corp TLS terminator (nginx LB).
- Region: prod-us-west provisioning VLAN

Steps to reproduce:
1) Boot device to network in provisioning VLAN and start autopilot flow.
2) Let SCCM task sequence run to 'Enroll device and request device certificate'.
3) Observe task sequence UI hang at 'Waiting for device certificate' for >30 minutes.

Observed logs / evidence:
- NDES access logs show connection from provisioning IPs but 404 responses for POST to /certsrv/mscep/mscep.dll for ~2026-03-10T08:12:00Z onwards.
- CA audit log shows incoming request with subject CN=AUTOMATED-REQUEST but CA rejects with 'Issuer mismatch: client bundle CN not in trust store'.
- Provisioning host syslog shows repeated retries every 2 minutes.
- Packet capture (PCAP) of one failed device shows TLS handshake to LB succeeded, HTTP 404 returned immediately.

Initial hypothesis:
- During the scheduled corp CA rotation last night a new CA bundle was deployed to the NGINX terminator but the NDES backend was not updated with the intermediate chain, causing CA validation failure.
- Alternatively SCEP path has been rewritten by recent ACL change on LB (ruleset id 2107) returning 404 for legacy hostnames used by SCCM task sequence.

Workarounds in place:
- Manual certificate provisioning: IT can temporarily run local cert enrollment via mmc or pre-stage device object in AD to bypass autoenroll. This is labor-intensive and only applied for high-priority hires.

Requested next steps:
- Triage and confirm whether LB ruleset or CA chain is root cause.
- If CA bundle mismatch, coordinate rollback or update NDES chain and redeploy.
- If LB ACL issue, revert ruleset 2107 or add explicit rule to allow /certsrv/mscep/* POSTs from provisioning VLAN.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:04 - Marco Ruiz: Picked up ticket. I can reproduce with a test T16 in the staging lab on prod-us-west VLAN. I see the same 404 in NGINX logs. Opening a runbook check with network infra.

2026-03-10 11:36 - Priya Singh (Network): LB ruleset 2107 applied during emergency config yesterday to migrate to LE certs. I can see a rewrite that returns 404 for unknown Host headers. Provisioning hosts use 'provisioning.corp.redwood' which was not included. Adding host alias now for a test.
2026-03-10 11:52 - Marco Ruiz: After Priya added host alias, same test device advanced past the 404 but now CA audit shows 'Issuer mismatch' errors. Suggests chain problem. Notifying Security/PKI.

2026-03-10 13:05 - Elena Morales (PKI): We rotated intermediate cert last night as part of scheduled rotation. Looks like the NDES server's chain bundle did not include the new intermediate. I'll prepare a hotfix to update the chain on the NDES host and schedule a quick restart of the service.

2026-03-11 09:18 - Marco Ruiz: Applied PKI chain update to ndes01.prod-us-west. Restarted ndes service. Ran a provisioning test; device successfully autoenrolled and obtained device cert. However, still seeing intermittent failures for a subset of Dell units (3/40). Collecting more logs.

2026-03-12 08:42 - Elena Morales (PKI): Follow-up: those Dell units were using a cached old image with hardcoded /certsrv hostnames. We pushed an image fix (v2026.03.1) to SCCM that corrects the host header. Requesting to keep ticket open until end of week to monitor batch provisioning.
2026-03-12 09:10 - Marco Ruiz: Monitoring ongoing. No new failures reported since image push. Marking as In Progress -> awaiting verification. Will update if anything reappears.
investigation_notes: NDES returned 404 due to LB host header rewrite; adding provisioning.corp.redwood alias allowed backend reachability.
CA audit logs indicated 'Issuer mismatch' caused by missing intermediate in NDES chain after rotation. PKI fix applied to ndes01 and ndes02 scheduled.
Residual failures traced to older SCCM image with hardcoded provisioning hostnames; new image update rolled out to task sequence and pushed as hotfix v2026.03.1.
No evidence of rogue certificates or compromise; change was operational error during CA rotation. Recommend improved pre-deploy validation for PKI chain on facade services.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: LB host alias added, NDES chain fixed, and SCCM image updated (v2026.03.1). Bulk provisioning resumed. Monitoring recommended for 72 hours.
resolution_notes:
Actions performed:
- Network: added host alias to LB to avoid 404s for provisioning hosts (temporary rule change).
- PKI: updated intermediate chain on NDES servers and restarted service (ndes01/ndes02).
- Imaging: patched SCCM task sequence image to correct hardcoded hostnames and bumped to v2026.03.1.
Follow-up items:
- Create post-change checklist for PKI rotations including NDES and LB validation (assigned to Elena Morales).
- Automate smoke test: small fleet provisioning test after CA rotation before full rollout (ticket INT-000000 to be created).
- Monitor provisioning metrics and open a follow-up retrospective with Network and PKI owners.
